terms.gloss: food, rations, feed (for animals as for people)
evidence: Varr. RR 2.9: Dīligenter ut habeat cibāria prōvidendum.
Col. 7.12.10: Cibāria ferē eadem sunt utrīque generī praebenda.
Col. 8.4.1: Cibāria gallīnīs praebentur optima pīnsitum hordeum et vicia
terms.comment: The farm writers’ word for what a dog or a hen is given to eat: Varro and Columella on the food of sheepdogs and house dogs, Columella on the feed of hens. Of a cat’s or a dog’s food at home, cibāria canis, cibāria fēlis. For what an animal finds or is given at one meal, cibus (see “food”); for fodder, pābulum (see “fodder”).

phrases.english: Pour the cat food into the bowl.

phrases.latin: Cibāria canis jam dēsunt; crās emenda sunt.
phrases.english: We’re out of dog food; we must buy some tomorrow.

phrases.latin: Cibātus canis propior hominis quam ovis. Pāscitur enim edūliīs et ossibus, nōn herbīs aut fronde. Dīligenter ut habeat cibāria prōvidendum.
phrases.english: A dog’s food is nearer a man’s than a sheep’s: he is fed on scraps and bones, not on grass or leaves. Care must be taken that he has his rations.

phrases.latin: Cibāria ferē eadem sunt utrīque generī praebenda.
phrases.english: Much the same food is to be given to both kinds (the farm dog and the shepherd’s dog).

sources: Lewis & Short: cibarius · Lewis & Short: cibatus
